So I've been playing a lot of old RPGs lately, partly as research for a throwback RPG I'm working on.

So for a while I was tag teaming Curse of the Azure Bonds (1989) and Baldur's Gate (1998).

I think both hold up rather well. I still enjoy the fundamental gameplay loop of Curse better. But I'm a sucker for exploring dungeons, mapping them out on graph paper, and turn based tactical combat. But Baldur's Gate definite wins in story, modern UI convenience, and sheer immersion. I forgot that in Baldur's Gate you hear the wildlife noises, see birds flying overhead, listen to your team make battle shouts, and bicker with one another. The feeling of being there is fantastic, even if I like the gameplay of Curse better.

But Curse doesn't hold up nearly as well as Pool of Radiance (1988) which I beat last year.

The last one I can remember is Super Mario Bros. 3, the All Stars version. The peak of the series honestly, the levels are better designed than World IMO and World only beats 3 in the number of secrets to hunt.
